identity.title: Fatigable ptosis on sustained upgaze (60 s)

technique.how: Measure baseline margin-reflex distance or note lid position, then have the patient fix on a target held above eye level and hold upgaze for 60 s (some protocols 2 min) without blinking excessively. Watch for progressive drooping of one or both lids or the appearance of diplopia; then let the eyes rest closed for 1-2 min and note recovery.
technique.prerequisites: Alert, cooperative patient; good lighting; compare with the ice-pack test if ptosis is present.

interpretation.positive_finding: Progressive lid droop (or diplopia) during sustained upgaze that improves with rest indicates fatigable neuromuscular weakness; sensitivity 0.80 for ocular MG in a neuro-ophthalmology cohort.
interpretation.negative_finding: No fatigability makes MG less likely but does not exclude it (specificity only 0.63; LR- about 0.32 computed); the ice-pack test (RCE LR+ 24, LR- 0.16) and antibody/electrophysiology testing carry more weight.
interpretation.pitfalls: Levator dehiscence, cranial nerve palsies and decompensated phorias can mimic; mild ptosis with low lid folds reduces detectability. The only accuracy estimate used a case definition that itself included upgaze fatigability (incorporation bias).
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: add ice-pack test, AChR antibodies and repetitive stimulation; screen for bulbar/respiratory involvement. Negative: MG still possible; pursue alternative causes of ptosis/diplopia.

estimates.target_condition: Ocular myasthenia gravis in patients referred for suspected MG; finding = fatigability on sustained upgaze
estimates.population: 138 patients referred to an academic neuro-ophthalmology clinic with suspected ocular MG over 9 years; 101 diagnosed with MG (95 ocular)
estimates.reference_standard: Clinical diagnosis (isolated ptosis/diplopia plus at least one abnormal confirmatory test: edrophonium, ice test, Cogan lid twitch, sustained-upgaze fatigability, AChR antibody, RNS decrement or single-fiber jitter)
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.80/(1-0.63) = 2.16; LR- = (1-0.80)/0.63 = 0.32; from reported sensitivity 0.80 and specificity 0.63 (no 2x2 counts in abstract)
estimates.quote: Test sensitivity/specificity in OMG was fatigability on sustained upgaze 0.80/0.63

sources.citation: Scherer K, Bedlack RS, Simel DL. Does this patient have myasthenia gravis? JAMA. 2005;293(15):1906-1914.
Mittal MK, Barohn RJ, Pasnoor M, et al. Ocular myasthenia gravis in an academic neuro-ophthalmology clinic: clinical features and therapeutic response. J Clin Neuromuscul Dis. 2012;13(1):46-52.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use a negative test to withhold work-up in a patient with bulbar symptoms or dyspnea; do not rely on it in uncooperative or drowsy patients.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Any ptosis with dysphagia, weak neck flexion, orthopnea or single breath count <20 suggests generalized/crisis MG: measure FVC and NIF and admit to monitored care.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Judgement of lid droop is subjective; agreement not reported. Measuring margin-reflex distance before and after (as in Kee 2020, PMID 30704861) makes the reading more objective.

extraction_notes: The 2005 RCE (abstract only; JAMA not in PMC) did not evaluate sustained upgaze; its quantified maneuvers are the ice test, peek sign, sleep/rest tests and edrophonium, so it is cited for context without numbers. The single accuracy estimate is from the abstract of Mittal 2012, a retrospective clinic series in which upgaze fatigability was itself part of the OMG case definition (incorporation bias inflates sensitivity); prevalence 101/138 = 0.73 computed from abstract counts. LRs computed from reported sens/spec. Kee 2020 (PMID 30704861) studies the ice-pack test performed after 2 min of sustained upgaze (sens 73.3%, spec 96.7%) - a combined test, not entered here. Handzic 2026 (PMID 40257852) lists the sustained upgaze test as a predictor but the abstract gives no item-level accuracy.
